standard_prerequisites: The one-sided classical sequent calculus G3c extended by the closed-surface cut rule, the height of a proof, and the cut rank of a cut inference, defined as the depth of its cut formula.

The height-preserving inversion lemma for the propositional rules of G3c and the inversion lemma for the quantifier rules of G3c, both proved in the sequent-calculus unit of the same source tree; the counted proof follows their case structure, which it restates in full.
The induction-with-varying-contexts convention: in height-preserving arguments the inductive hypothesis is stated for all contexts, not just the ones occurring in the given proof.
core_obligations: State and prove the inversion lemma for G3c with closed-surface cut: if the extended system proves the conclusion of a logical rule R other than right-exists or left-forall, then it proves each premise of R; moreover the transformed premise proofs neither raise the proof height nor change the number or the ranks of cut inferences.

Carry out the induction on the proof height: the base case replaces an axiom by another axiom, so both invariants are trivial; the case where the last rule is R itself takes the immediate subproofs as the wanted premise proofs; every other case applies the inductive hypothesis to the immediate subproofs and re-applies the last rule, and the two invariants transfer to the whole proof.

Verify the cut case: the inductive hypothesis applies to the subproofs above the topmost cut inference, which remain proofs of instances of the same rule's conclusion, and the two transformed premise proofs are recombined with a single cut inference of the same rank, as displayed for the left-and rule.
proof_roadmap: Follow the case taxonomy of the sequent-calculus inversion proofs, checking the two extra invariants (height non-increase, cut count and rank invariance) in each case.

The cut case is the only genuinely new case; demonstrate it in full for the left-and rule with both displayed derivations, and note that the remaining logical rules are instances of the same shape (a single-premise rule yields one transformed premise proof combined by the same cut inference).
difficulty_reason: A structural adaptation of an inversion induction to the proof system with cut: every case of the underlying inversion proof must be re-verified against two extra invariants (proof height and the number and ranks of cut inferences), and the genuinely new cut case needs the recombination derivation; the bookkeeping discipline across all cases is the difficulty.
